events.title: King Vitiges and the Ostrogoths begin the siege of Rome
events.description: A numerically superior Ostrogothic army under Vitiges laid siege to Rome, held by Byzantine forces under Belisarius, who with his bucellarii was almost cut off outside the Flaminian Gate. The year-long siege shaped the rest of the Gothic War.
events.html: A numerically superior Ostrogothic army under Vitiges laid siege to Rome, held by Byzantine forces under Belisarius, who with his bucellarii was almost cut off outside the Flaminian Gate. The year-long siege shaped the rest of the Gothic War.

events.title: Louis V becomes the last Carolingian King of the Franks
events.description: On the death of his father Lothair, Louis V became sole king. He died a year later without an heir, and the nobles elected Hugh Capet, founder of the Capetian dynasty.
events.html: On the death of his father Lothair, Louis V became sole king. He died a year later without an heir, and the nobles elected Hugh Capet, founder of the Capetian dynasty.

events.title: Skanderbeg gathers Albanian nobles in the League of Lezhë
events.description: Under Venetian patronage, Skanderbeg summoned Albanian noblemen to Lezhë, where they formed a military alliance against the Ottomans. It was the first time that much of Albania was united under a single leader, and his army fought the Ottomans until 1468.

events.title: Swiss defeat Charles the Bold at Grandson
events.description: The Swiss Confederates routed the Burgundian army near Lake Neuchâtel and seized Charles the Bold's rich baggage train. Further defeats at Morat and Nancy destroyed Burgundian power.
events.html: The Swiss Confederates routed the Burgundian army near Lake Neuchâtel and seized Charles the Bold's rich baggage train. Further defeats at Morat and Nancy destroyed Burgundian power.

events.title: Jefferson signs the act banning the importation of slaves
events.description: The law prohibited bringing enslaved people into the United States from 1 January 1808, the earliest date the Constitution allowed. Smuggling and the domestic slave trade continued.
events.html: The law prohibited bringing enslaved people into the United States from 1 January 1808, the earliest date the Constitution allowed. Smuggling and the domestic slave trade continued.

events.title: Texas declares independence from Mexico
events.description: Delegates at Washington-on-the-Brazos adopted a declaration of independence, creating the Republic of Texas. Victory at San Jacinto in April secured it, and Texas joined the United States in 1845.
events.html: Delegates at Washington-on-the-Brazos adopted a declaration of independence, creating the Republic of Texas. Victory at San Jacinto in April secured it, and Texas joined the United States in 1845.

events.title: Congress creates the Nevada and Dakota territories
events.description: Two days before leaving office, President James Buchanan signed acts organising the Nevada and Dakota territories. Nevada's silver helped finance the Union, and it became a state in 1864.
events.html: Two days before leaving office, President James Buchanan signed acts organising the Nevada and Dakota territories. Nevada's silver helped finance the Union, and it became a state in 1864.

events.title: Rutherford B. Hayes declared winner of the disputed 1876 election
events.description: Congress confirmed the Electoral Commission's award of all disputed votes to Hayes, giving him victory by one electoral vote. Under the Compromise of 1877, federal troops left the South.
events.html: Congress confirmed the Electoral Commission's award of all disputed votes to Hayes, giving him victory by one electoral vote. Under the Compromise of 1877, federal troops left the South.

events.title: D. H. Lawrence dies in the south of France
events.description: The author of 'Sons and Lovers' and 'Lady Chatterley's Lover' died of tuberculosis at Vence, aged 44. 'Lady Chatterley' was not published openly in Britain until the 1960 obscenity trial.
events.html: The author of 'Sons and Lovers' and 'Lady Chatterley's Lover' died of tuberculosis at Vence, aged 44. 'Lady Chatterley' was not published openly in Britain until the 1960 obscenity trial.

events.title: Battle of the Bismarck Sea begins
events.description: American and Australian aircraft attacked a Japanese convoy bound for New Guinea, sinking all eight transports and four destroyers over three days. About 3,000 Japanese troops died.
events.html: American and Australian aircraft attacked a Japanese convoy bound for New Guinea, sinking all eight transports and four destroyers over three days. About 3,000 Japanese troops died.

events.title: Concorde makes its first flight
events.description: Test pilot André Turcat flew the Anglo-French supersonic airliner prototype from Toulouse. Concorde entered passenger service in 1976 and flew until 2003.

song: Samba musicians of Rio de Janeiro (the circle at Tia Ciata's house)
Made up in 1916 by musicians meeting in Tia Ciata's backyard, it is counted as the first samba ever recorded in Brazil.
